Subject: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - integration follow-up

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you and the FinPay team earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so your network and security folks have what they need to evaluate the integration: 

What we heard from FinPay:
- You want private connectivity from your VPC to Redwood's service (private deployment path) for production traffic.
- Primary concerns: stable egress IPs for allowlisting, DNS resolution of Redwood endpoints, and mutual TLS for service-to-service authentication.
- Timeline: aiming for a pilot in June, production H2.

Redwood integration options (high level):
1) VPC endpoints / private egress — we can expose dedicated VPC endpoints with fixed egress IPs for your region.
2) IP allowlist — we provide a list of egress ranges (or a small set of NAT IPs) you can add to your allowlist.
3) mTLS — supported for our Private deployments; we can provision certs or validate client certs from your CA.
4) DNS & routing — we support DNS records you can resolve privately via conditional forwards to our endpoints.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- I'll loop in Jonas (network engineering) with a technical checklist and a sample allowlist/template.
- Alex to share FinPay's network contact + any current NAT/egress IP constraints and whether you prefer client-cert mTLS or a TLS-with-jwt approach.
- Exchange a draft mutual-action-plan (timeline + owners).

I've attached: Redwood VPC integration guide and a simple network diagram.

Would you be available next Wednesday (Apr 7) for a 30-min integration session (FinPay network + Redwood infra)?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

Hi Alex / Lauren —

Thanks for the context. A few technical clarifications ahead of Apr 7: 

1) Egress IPs / allowlist
- For Redwood Private we can provide a small set of static IPs (usually 2-64 per region) that originate traffic to your services. If you prefer, we can also provide a CIDR block for your firewall team.
- We'll export a CSV allowlist template with columns: region, ip, protocol, port, purpose (I'll attach the template).

2) VPC endpoints & routing
- We can support two patterns: (A) Private link-style endpoints (peerings/endpoint service) or (B) NAT egress with static IPs. The best fit depends on your infra (do you allow VPC peering vs endpoints?).
- If using DNS conditional forwarding, we'll provide the FQDNs to include and TTL recommendations.

3) mTLS & auth
- mTLS: we support client cert validation against your CA (you can either upload the CA bundle or use ACME/provisioned certs in coordination).
- Alternative: TLS + signed JWTs (for per-request auth) — supported by our API and often simpler for rotation.

4) Embeddings/rerankers and structured output routing
- For embedding calls, traffic patterns are similar; we'll recommend keeping embedding traffic on the same private path to minimize egress complexity.
- If you plan to use rerankers (server-side), we can co-locate those services in the same private network to avoid cross-VPC calls.

Please find the allowlist template attached (vpc-endpoints-allowlist-template.csv) and a short checklist: what we need from FinPay before the call:
- Primary network contact (Mike) — done.
- Your preferred pattern (VPC endpoint vs static NAT) — if undecided we'll discuss on the call.
- Any firewall/proxy egress inspection that would break mTLS (TLS-terminating proxy) — please flag if present.

I'll be on the Apr 7 10am PT call.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Staff Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
